mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off sentiment that compresses equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by more than 0.25 percentage points
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns during triggered events are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed prior quarter median in 70% of tightening events.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signal disinflation, which reduces policy rate expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months by more than 0.3% from the prior month's value
failure_condition: In regimes where CPIAUCSL declines are not accompanied by lower 10-year yields or lower VIX, 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat over the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs per month coincides with investor optimism, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 by at least 50,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: During periods of high uncertainty (VIX > 20), 20-day forward returns after such PAYEMS spikes are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior quarter's median indicates weakening demand, which reduces future earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below its prior quarter median by more than 2 points
regime_hint: early sign of soft landing failure
failure_condition: Over 100 such INDPRO contractions, 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales proxy (HOUST) of at least 3% suggests waning consumer demand, which depresses corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for two consecutive months by at least 3% from prior month
failure_condition: During periods of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 0.2%), such declines do not precede negative 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 1-month moving averages signals a resilient demand cycle, forecasting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST > HOUST[1m] and INDPRO > INDPRO[1m] for the current month
regime_hint: coordinated strength across supply and demand sectors
failure_condition: In regimes with elevated financial stress (UNRATE < 3%), this interaction does not predict positive 60-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates a labor market cooling, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 4.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of high monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 5%), UNRATE stays above 4.5% but 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months in a tightening regime is interpreted as policy accommodation ending, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS is above 5% for the preceding month
failure_condition: In regimes where CPIAUCSL remains below 2% but FEDFUNDS does not rise, 60-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05).
